item.title: Time to Confront Escalating Russia-Iran Intelligence Cooperation
item.description: Russia-Iran intelligence and technology cooperation is escalating. It’s time for the United States to better prioritize confronting it.

item.title: Bridging the Gulf? Thailand and Cambodia Turn to UNCLOS
item.description: Thailand and Cambodia begin compulsory conciliation talks.

item.title: Is an Energy Truce Viable in the Ukraine War?
item.description: An energy truce in the Ukraine war before winter would serve Kyiv, Moscow, and global markets, yet past pauses have repeatedly broken down. A deal can hold only with a narrow target registry, independent satellite-based verification, and graduated responses to violations.

item.title: What’s Next? Part I
item.description: In this week’s column, Bill Reinsch discusses what U.S. trade policy might look like after the Trump administration.

item.title: EU-China Relations Face an Existential Test, but Escalation Is Not Inevitable
item.description: On July 28, the Chinese Ministry of Commerce published its “Position on the So-called Excess Capacity Issue” to rebut foreign concerns about Chinese overcapacity, signaling a renewal of tensions for upcoming EU-China trade negotiations.

item.title: Wrong Place, Right Line: Interregional Transmission as a Hedge Against Uncertain Large Loads
item.description: Data centers and other large loads are reshaping U.S. electricity demand, but where and when they will materialize remains deeply uncertain. This piece argues interregional transmission offers a resilient hedge against that uncertainty in transmission planning.

item.title: The Golden Dome for America Initiative
item.description: Missiles and drones have become weapons of choice. Missile defenses have, in turn, become foundational to deterrence and defense. The need to revolutionize our nation's approach to homeland air and missile defense capabilities is strategically necessary and long overdue.

item.title: U.S. Enforcement Against the European Hamas–Muslim Brotherhood Network Since October 7, 2023
item.description: Historically, European governments have failed to adequately combat the Muslim Brotherhood. The Trump administration’s renewed focus on the group presents an opportunity for European states to target their own Muslim Brotherhood network more effectively.

item.title: Takeaways from the Trump-Xi White House Summit
item.description: CSIS experts assess the outcomes of the Trump-Xi White House summit in September 2026 and what it means for the future of U.S.-China relations.
